stimuli.title: Eight boxes labelled Meera, Deepa, Lata, Gita, Kiran, Riya, Aditi, Tara are stacked one above another. Position 1 is at the bottom and position 8 at the top.
stimuli.body:
Use all the following clues:
• Gita occupies position 6 from the bottom.
• Exactly 5 boxes are between Lata and Tara.
• Riya is below Aditi.
• Meera is in an odd-numbered position from the bottom.
• Meera and Deepa are adjacent boxes.
• Exactly 1 box is between Lata and Gita.
• Exactly 2 boxes are between Lata and Aditi.

questions.stem:
In a substitution language, each word has one distinct code. Code order is arbitrary.
savings banking digital = to lu ka
savings growth secure = pa re to
banking growth credit = pa ka su
digital secure credit = su re lu
savings banking credit = ka su to
What is the code for “growth”?
questions.explanation: Answer: pa. Compare the intersections of the coded lines. The complete consistent mapping is: savings = to, banking = ka, digital = lu, growth = pa, secure = re, credit = su.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 131 km south, turns left and walks 225 km, then turns left and walks 11 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 255. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 120 km along the initial direction and 225 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(120² + 225²) = 255 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 22 km south, turns right and walks 24 km, then turns right and walks 4 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 30. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 18 km along the initial direction and 24 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(18² + 24²) = 30 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 53 km east, turns left and walks 108 km, then turns left and walks 8 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 117. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 45 km along the initial direction and 108 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(45² + 108²) = 117 km.

questions.stem: E is the mother of D. H is the son of D. A is the father of D. How is H related to A?
questions.explanation: Answer: Grandson. A is a parent of D, and H is D’s son. Hence H is A’s grandchild.

questions.stem: D is the brother of B. B is the mother of A. H is the father of D and B. How is D related to A?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. D is the brother of A’s mother B. Therefore D is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: F is the only daughter of A. A is the father of F. D is the son of F. G is the sister of A. How is A related to D?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. A is the father of F, and F is D’s mother. Thus A is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: In a queue of 49 candidates, a candidate is 21th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 26. New front rank = 21+3 = 24. Back rank = 49 − 24 + 1 = 26.

questions.stem: In a queue of 58 candidates, a candidate is 18th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 37. New front rank = 18+4 = 22. Back rank = 58 − 22 + 1 = 37.

II. y² − 26y + 168 = 0
Choose the strongest relationship that holds for all possible root pairings.
options: x = y or relationship cannot be determined
questions.explanation: Answer: x < y. Factor I: roots 1, 11. Factor II: roots 12, 14. Compare all four pairings to obtain x < y.

questions.stem: An item costs ₹1250. It is marked above cost and sold at a 10% discount on marked price, earning 12% profit. Find the marked price (₹, to two decimals).
questions.explanation: Answer: 1555.56. Selling price = 1250 × 112/100. Marked price = selling price ÷ 0.9 = 1555.56.

questions.stem: A can finish a job in 20 days and B in 30 days. They work together for 2 days, then B leaves. How many more days does A need? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 16.67. Use 60 work units. Rates: A = 3, B = 2 units/day. Remaining = 60 − 2×5. Divide by A’s rate 3.

questions.stem: A boat travels 320 km downstream and the same distance upstream. Its still-water speed is 18 km/h and stream speed is 2 km/h. Find the total time (hours).
A invests ₹20000 for 12 months. B invests ₹40000 for 5 months. Total profit is ₹48400. Find B’s share (₹).
questions.explanation: Answer: 22000. Capital-time ratio = 12 : 10. B’s share = total × 10/(22) = 22000.

questions.stem: What is the difference (₹) between compound interest and simple interest on ₹23000 at 10% per annum for 2 years, compounded annually?
questions.explanation: Answer: 230. For 2 years, CI − SI = P(r/100)² = 23000 × (10/100)².

questions.stem: A vessel contains 75 litres of milk and water in ratio 3:2. How many litres of pure milk must be added to make the ratio 2:1?
questions.explanation: Answer: 15. Milk = 3V/5, water = 2V/5. Solve (3V/5 + x)/(2V/5) = 2; x = V/5 = 15.

questions.stem: The average of 33 numbers is 45. One number, 57, is replaced and the average rises by 7. What is the new number?
questions.explanation: Answer: 288. Total increases by 33 × 7. New number = 57 + 231.

questions.stem: A father is three times as old as his daughter. After 3 years, their combined age will be 86 years. Find the father’s present age.
questions.explanation: Answer: 60. Let daughter’s age be x. Father is 3x. 4x + 6 = 86; x = 20, so father = 60.

questions.stem: A train of length 240 m crosses a 150 m platform at 72 km/h. Find crossing time in seconds (to two decimals).
A village has 3000 registered customers. This increases by 20% in year 1 and decreases by 20% in year 2. What is the final number?
questions.explanation: Answer: 2880. Apply successive factors: 3000 × 120/100 × 80/100.
